messages.subject: plotting subset of data common to experimental replicates
parts:
Hi,

Having issues trying to plot a subset of data points common to series of experimental replicates. I have a large data frame (nrow=16000) consisting of three experiments. I would like to plot (mean, diff) as a facet_grid for each exp (1, 2, 3). I want to color the points in experiments 1 and 2 that have a certain value in experiment 3. For instance, if diff > 0 and mean > 0 in plate_round_3, colour those points blue for round 3, round 2 and round 1, all other points leave black.

I can do this in plot(), but can't manage the syntax in ggplot2. The plot() results looks like this:

Thanks,
-dave

messages.subject: Re: plotting subset of data common to experimental replicates
parts:
Ista posted earlier today with an example of subsetting that I would use in this case. Create a separate data frame for each type of situation you want and then use that data frame for plotting via separate calls to geom_point. Something like (where you would update all of these conditions and colors with what you actually want):

diff_condition <- df$diff > 0
mean_condition <- df$mean > 0
df1 <- df[diff_condition, ]
df2 <- df[mean_condition, ]
df3 <- df[!(diff_condition | mean_condition), ]

p <- ggplot(df3, aes(x, y)) + 
geom_point() + 
geom_point(data = df1, color = "blue") +
geom_point(data = df2, color = "red")
